messages:
kevin: Customer ACME via ticket #5682 reports missing audit events in our SIEM export (Splunk). They say uploads and KMS operations between 2025-11-02T14:00Z and 2025-11-02T16:30Z are absent. They provided sample event_ids: evt_9a1, evt_9a7, evt_9b3. Can someone triage?

anna: Ack — passing to eng-security + SRE. Do we have the raw export logs for that window? @sre-lucy can you check the forwarder? :eyes: 

sre-lucy: Checking now. Quick notes: our SIEM forwarder (kafka->splunk HEC) has two components: exporter service (kafka consumer + transform) and delivery worker (HEC client). No alerts in pagerduty during that window. Looking at exporter offsets for topic audit-exports: there is an offset gap on partition 2 around 2025-11-02T14:22Z. Pulling logs.

kevin: The customer included a snippet of expected schema: `{"ts":"2025-11-02T14:05:23Z","event_type":"file.upload","user":"u-1234","event_id":"evt_9a1","resource":"s3:bucket/xyz"}`. They said those aren't in Splunk.

eng-security-jordan: If offsets jumped we may have had a transient rebalancing. Two quick questions: 1) Were those events ever ingested by kafka? 2) If ingested, did exporter drop them during transform (schema validation) or during HEC publish?

sre-lucy: Ran `kafka-avro-console-consumer --from-beginning --partition 2 --offset 24000 --max-messages 2000 --topic audit-exports | grep evt_9a1` — no hits for evt_9a1/9a7, but found evt_9b3 in nearby offsets. Looks like evt_9a1/9a7 never made it into topic partition 2; need to check producer logs (audit-service).

kevin: Customer asserts they saw success responses from API for those upload operations. They included request_ids: req_33fa, req_33fb. We have an ingestion path: api -> audit-service (producer) -> kafka -> exporter -> Splunk.

anna: Can we confirm audit-service produced messages for those request_ids? If not, maybe producer crashed or KMS/HSM step blocked final write and we still returned success (bad).

eng-security-jordan: Also verify retention: customer asked about missing schema fields like `user_ip` and `kms_key`. We recently introduced schema v2 where `kms_key` is optional and may be stripped for privacy if KMS policy flagged. Could that explain missing fields? However that wouldn't remove entire events.

sre-lucy: Tail from audit-service around 2025-11-02T14:00: `kubectl logs -n prod audit-service-78f4 --since=3h | grep "req_33f"` shows entries for req_33fa and req_33fb with final status=200 and a produced=true log line. But the producer uses an async buffer — I see an error: `WARN producer-buffer: dropped 12 messages due to buffer_full`. Timestamp 2025-11-02T14:21:35Z. That matches the offset gap window.

kevin: So producer dropped messages under backpressure. That would explain absence in kafka. Customer is understandably upset. What are mitigation options?

eng-security-jordan: Short-term: offer customer an ad-hoc resync — we can generate a manual export for the time range from audit-service persistence (audit events are stored for 90 days in our primary DB) and push to their Splunk HEC as a one-off. Need customer permission. Medium-term: fix producer buffer sizing and surface dropped metrics as alertable (SLO).

anna: Also need to document retention guarantees: current policy is 90 days for audit raw events in DB, Splunk export is best-effort streaming; we should clarify in docs. Customer asked if KMS/HSM logs could be withheld — eng-security-jordan said only if redaction policy applied, otherwise retained.

sre-lucy: Action items I can take now: 1) run resync export for ticket #5682 time range and push to their HEC as adhoc (will include events we still have) 2) bump producer buffer and add alert on `producer-buffer.dropped > 0` but will schedule after change window. I'll open PR and link here.

kevin: Please include exact repro steps for us to send to customer and include the exported file (masked PHI) if they approve. Also ask if they want KMS key IDs in payload or redacted.

eng-security-jordan: For compliance note: if we re-send events containing KMS key ids we must ensure KMS access controls are met. Confirm with compliance. Also we should capture an internal timeline for incident postmortem (who/what/when).

support-bot: Ticket #5682 status changed to escalated -> eng-security. SLA pause requested by kevin.

kevin: Thanks. I'll message the customer with a proposed remediation: (a) we will run an adhoc export from our audit DB for the window and deliver to their Splunk HEC, (b) we will add monitoring/alerts and a config change to prevent future drops, (c) we'll provide a short postmortem and confirm retention/schema behavior. Will ask for explicit consent to resend events containing kms_key.

anna: Nice. @sre-lucy please paste the `kubectl` commands and the PR link once ready so I can copy into the ticket.

sre-lucy: Commands: ```
# search prod audit-service logs for request ids
kubectl logs -n prod deploy/audit-service --since=4h | grep -E "req_33f|evt_9a1|producer-buffer"
# create adhoc export (internal tool)
./tools/audit-export --start "2025-11-02T14:00:00Z" --end "2025-11-02T16:30:00Z" --out /tmp/acme_export.ndjson
# push to Splunk HEC
curl -k -H "Authorization: Splunk <HEC_TOKEN>" --data-binary @/tmp/acme_export.ndjson https://splunk.acme/hec/1/event
```

kevin: Perfect — I'll draft a customer message and post here before sending. :thumbsup:

anna: Keep thread updated with PR and export confirmation. After we deliver, create a short postmortem and link to incident tracker.

eng-security-jordan: One last ask — include the event schema we send in the export in the ticket. Current canonical schema v1/v2 lives in internal docs: https://internal.redwood.io/docs/audit/schema. Make sure to note fields that may be redacted for compliance.

kevin: Will do. End of thread for now.
